posts.title: GaitAI begins ISO 13485 readiness assessment for medical-grade gait analytics
posts.summary: An important milestone on our path to certified medical use — GaitAI has formally begun ISO 13485 quality-management readiness for its Care vertical.
posts.body:
## What this means

ISO 13485 is the global quality-management standard for medical devices and medical software. Beginning readiness is the first formal step toward GaitAI Care being deployable in clinical environments such as hospitals, rehabilitation centers and elderly-care facilities.

## What we're working on

- Documented quality-management system across product, engineering, data and clinical operations.
- Risk-management process per ISO 14971 for every Care feature.
- Clinical evaluation plan for fall-risk prediction and gait-based mobility scoring.
- Post-market surveillance plan covering edge devices and cloud analytics.

## Why this matters

Movement intelligence can only protect lives if it is auditable, safe and trustworthy. Our long-term mission is to make GaitAI Care a tool every clinician, family and rehabilitation specialist can rely on — and that begins with the right quality foundation.

> "Building movement intelligence for healthcare is a privilege. ISO 13485 is the floor we choose to build above."

We'll share periodic updates here as we progress through audit and certification.
posts.author: GaitAI Compliance

posts.title: Early Parkinsonian gait detection via multi-view pose & temporal symmetry
posts.summary: A look at our internal research on detecting early Parkinsonian movement patterns months before clinical diagnosis — using multi-view 2D pose plus temporal symmetry features.
posts.body:
## Background

Parkinson's disease has well-documented gait markers — reduced arm swing, asymmetric stride, freezing episodes, postural micro-instabilities — that often appear long before formal diagnosis.

## Our approach

We combine:

- **Multi-view 2D pose** estimation at 30fps from standard RGB cameras.
- **Temporal symmetry features** computed across left/right limbs over rolling windows.
- A **probabilistic risk score** designed to surface change-over-time rather than absolute diagnosis.

## Early findings

In our internal dataset of synthetic and consented real-world walking sequences, the symmetry-decay feature alone produced strong separation between baseline and induced asymmetry. We're actively expanding the dataset with research partners.

## What's next

GaitAI is **not** a diagnostic device. The objective is to surface early signals that prompt human clinical review. The next phase is multi-site validation with neurology research groups.

If you're a clinician or research lab working on movement-linked neurological conditions, [reach out](#contact) — we're actively forming research collaborations.

posts.title: GaitAI Care preview launches for select early partners
posts.summary: The first private preview of GaitAI Care — designed for elderly fall-risk prediction and family-grade movement monitoring — is now in the hands of early partners.
posts.body:
Today we are opening the first private preview of **GaitAI Care** to a small group of design partners: two rehabilitation centers, one senior-living provider and three family-care pilot homes.

## What's in the preview

- Continuous gait observation from a single ceiling-mounted RGB sensor.
- Daily mobility, balance and stability scoring for each resident.
- Family-friendly alerts when fall-risk indicators cross a personalized threshold.
- Clinician-grade longitudinal dashboards.

## What we're learning

Early feedback has been clear: families don't want more alerts, they want **fewer, more meaningful ones**. We're tuning our risk model to reduce noise and surface only changes worth a conversation.

If you operate an elderly-care facility, rehabilitation program or research home and want to join the next wave of design partners, [get in touch](#contact).

posts.title: GaitAI Edge SDK — getting started
posts.summary: A walkthrough of the GaitAI Edge SDK — how to run gait pose, identity and risk inference on a single edge device with sub-40ms latency.
posts.body:
## Install

```bash
pip install gaitai-edge
```

## Hello, gait

```python
from gaitai_edge import GaitStream

stream = GaitStream.from_camera(0, model="gaitai-base-v1")
for frame in stream:
    print(frame.identity_score, frame.fall_risk, frame.cadence)
```

## What you get per frame

- 17-keypoint 2D pose (COCO format)
- A rolling identity signature
- Balance, cadence and symmetry signals
- A bounded fall-risk score in [0, 1]

## Requirements

- Python 3.10+
- A CUDA-capable GPU **or** Apple Silicon (Metal)
- 200MB free disk

## Next

Read the [model card](#) and the [privacy whitepaper](#). Reach out to ship Edge SDK to your fleet at scale.

posts.title: Why movement intelligence is the next biometric frontier
posts.summary: Face, fingerprint and voice have limits. Movement is universal, ambient, hard to spoof — and reveals more than identity. A short essay on why it matters.
posts.body:
Face works in good light. Fingerprint needs a touch. Voice fails in a crowd. Each of the dominant biometrics has a useful surface and a clear edge it falls off.

**Movement is different.** It works from a distance. It works from above, from below, from the side. It works in poor light, in masks, in heavy clothing. It works for the consenting and — uncomfortably — for the non-consenting. It can be a tool of safety and it can be a tool of surveillance. That is why how it is built matters.

GaitAI is built around two beliefs:

1. Movement intelligence will be the next dominant ambient biometric.
2. It must be built with privacy-by-design, explainability and the dignity of the observed person as first-class concerns.

The reason GaitAI splits its platform into **Secure** and **Care** is exactly because the same underlying signal — *how a person moves* — answers two different questions:

- *Who is this person?* (Secure)
- *Is this person okay?* (Care)

Both questions matter. We intend to answer them with the same intelligence and the same standard of care.
posts.author: GaitAI

posts.title: Q2 showcase: 5-figure gait sequence demo
posts.summary: Watch our Q2 internal showcase — five animated gait sequences rendered in real-time on a single edge device.
posts.body:
Our Q2 showcase brought our hero demo to life: **five concurrent gait sequences**, each pulling identity, balance and cadence from a single edge inference pass.

## What we wanted to prove

- One model, five concurrent subjects, sub-40ms per frame.
- Clean identity separation even when subjects walked the same path.
- Per-subject longitudinal scoring that survives occlusion.

## What we learned

The biggest insight came from **occlusion recovery** — when subject 3 walks behind subject 4 for ~12 frames, the identity signature must hold. Our temporal pose buffer made the difference.

## Watch

A trimmed version of the showcase is available on request. [Get in touch](#contact) if you'd like a walkthrough.

posts.title: Designing for the way people actually walk
posts.summary: Real gait is messy — phones in hand, bags on shoulders, limps, hurry. A short piece on building movement models that respect how people really move.
posts.body:
Lab walks are clean. Real walks are not.

People walk while texting, while carrying groceries, while herding a toddler. They limp on a bad knee, speed up when late, slow down on ice. **A movement model that only works on a clean treadmill walk is a demo, not a product.**

## Three things we design around

- **Load and occlusion.** Bags, coats and crowds hide limbs. Our temporal buffer keeps an identity signature alive through short gaps.
- **Intent, not just identity.** *How* someone moves often matters more than *who* they are — hesitation, instability, a sudden change in cadence.
- **Dignity.** The observed person rarely consents to being measured. That constraint shapes every default we ship.

## The takeaway

If you build for the idealized walk, you fail in the real hallway. We build for the hallway.
posts.author: GaitAI

posts.title: Privacy by default, not by paperwork
posts.summary: Privacy isn't a policy PDF — it's an architecture decision. How GaitAI keeps movement data minimal, on-device and explainable from the first frame.
posts.body:
Most privacy promises live in a document nobody reads. We'd rather they live in the architecture.

## What 'by default' means here

- **On-device first.** Pose, identity and risk inference run at the edge. Raw video doesn't need to leave the camera.
- **Signals, not footage.** We persist bounded scores and signatures, not pixels, wherever the use case allows.
- **Explainable outputs.** Every risk score can point to the features that moved it — no black-box alerts.

## Why it matters

Movement is an ambient biometric: it works without anyone opting in. The only ethical response is to collect the least, keep it the shortest time, and make every output legible to the people it affects.

That's not paperwork. That's the build.

posts.title: June 2026 update: faster edge inference & a new balance signal
posts.summary: This month: a 22% latency cut on the edge runtime, a new lateral-balance signal in Care, and expanded multi-subject tracking in Secure.
posts.body:
A quick roundup of what shipped this month.

## Faster edge runtime

The v1.4 edge runtime cuts per-frame latency by **22%** on Apple Silicon and mid-range Jetson boards — more headroom for multi-subject scenes.

## New lateral-balance signal (Care)

Care now surfaces a **lateral sway** signal alongside cadence and symmetry, an early indicator we've found useful for fall-risk trends.

## Multi-subject tracking (Secure)

Secure now holds clean identity separation for up to **eight** concurrent subjects in a single frame, up from five.

## Coming next

We're piloting longitudinal dashboards with two design partners and expanding the consented research dataset. More soon.

posts.title: Subscriber deep-dive: how gait embeddings stay stable across cameras
posts.summary: A subscriber-only technical deep-dive into the contrastive training and normalization tricks that keep GaitAI identity embeddings stable across camera angles.
posts.body:
> This is a subscriber-only post — the discussion below it is reserved for GaitAI subscribers, so you'll see the locked state instead of the comment box.

## The problem

The same person filmed from two angles produces very different raw pose sequences. A naive embedding drifts badly across cameras.

## What keeps it stable

- **Contrastive training** across synthetic multi-view pairs of the same walk.
- **View-invariant normalization** of the skeleton before embedding.
- **Temporal pooling** that averages out per-frame noise while preserving rhythm.

## Result

Cross-camera identity matching holds up far better than per-frame matching, which is what makes ambient, multi-camera deployments practical.

Full benchmark tables are in the subscriber appendix.
